evidence.summary: Process lifecycle active and retained counts are bounded at 16 and 128; TaskScope runs bounded artifact calls on host threads and joins them.
Newer generations supersede and reap stale in-flight verification without a steady-state per-job status poll.

reproduction.instructions: Run cargo test -p mncs-model process_runtime::tests and the focused Forge supersession test; scope behavior is separately exercised by mncs-embed.

summary: Profile 0.18 TaskScope provides bounded joined host-thread concurrency, while the process runtime admits at most 16 active executions and retains at most 128 terminal handles; the Forge continuous path uses event-driven supersession. These do not provide source-level general scheduling or async/thread primitives, so the imported concurrency pressure remains partially open.

workaround.description: Actual concurrent scheduling remains an embed/runtime realization; MNCS source-level general scheduler and async/thread syntax are still absent.
